Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. I focused this email on the operational constraints you shared and the immediate asks we agreed to validate.

Key pain & goals you mentioned:
- Strict 95th-pctl latency target ~150ms for short-form completion path (<=512 tokens)
- Sustained throughput target: 120 req/s per region during peak (US-East, US-West)
- Burst headroom to 400 req/s for 30s windows for promotional events
- Data residency: inference in US regions only, PII never leaves customer VPC for private deployment
- Model family: you plan to evaluate Llama-compat 70B (quantized) plus a smaller 13B variant for fallbacks

Constraints that will impact topology and cost:
- KV/cache hit rate expected ~30-40% initially (you anticipate improving to ~65% after schema optimizations)
- Average prompt length today is 120 tokens; long-tail up to 2k tokens for diagnostics
- On-call window: 24x7 SLA required; you also asked about runbook handoff and playbook for regional failover

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
1) Redwood to propose a deployment topology and perf baseline for the 70B + 13B combo (Diego) — draft by EOD 11/19
2) EdgeOps infra team to share traffic shape CSV + sample prompts (Alyssa/Tom) — requested today; target 11/19
3) Marcus to produce a committed capacity estimate and high-level pricing band (Marcus) — by 11/20
4) Joint follow-up: 60-minute infra deep-dive with EdgeOps SREs + Redwood runtime (all) — propose slots for 11/23

Attachments I'm sending with this note: edgeops-inference-profiles.xlsx (format: traffic shape + token histograms), redwood-dedicated-config.yml (initial config sketch). I'll also add a short MAP draft after Marcus' pricing note.

Let me know if I missed anything. If the latency target below 150ms is a hard blocker please call it out — that will change the recommended topology (more dedicated GPUs / smaller model fan-out).

Best,
Diego Fernandez

Alyssa / Tom —

Below is a concise technical proposal to meet the targets you outlined. This is a starting point; we can iterate on the deep-dive with your SREs.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Redwood Dedicated pool per region (US-EAST, US-WEST) with cross-region fallback and automatic routing by latency SLO.
- Primary model: quantized 70B on A100-H20-class nodes with continuous KV caching for common prefixes; fallback 13B on T4 or A10 nodes for cost-sensitive traffic.
- Batching: dynamic batching with target batch size 16, max 64, timeout 10ms for user-facing path; background jobs use larger batches (256) and relaxed timeout.
- KV cache: default TTL 300s, adaptive eviction for hot keys. Expect >2x p95 reduction in token compute for hit cases.
- Autoscaling: predictive baseline to maintain 95th <=150ms; burst pool of pre-warmed nodes to cover 400 req/s spikes for ~30s windows.

Sizing back-of-envelope (initial):
- US-EAST Dedicated pool: min 8 GPUs (baseline), target 18 GPUs, burst capacity up to 30 GPUs.
- US-WEST Dedicated pool: min 6 GPUs, target 12 GPUs, burst up to 24 GPUs.
- These figures assume 30-40% initial KV hit rate and average prompt 120 tokens; improving cache hit to 65% drops baseline GPUs by ~35%.

Operational notes / considerations:
- Cold-start policy: keep a small set of warm replicas for the 70B to avoid long tail cold latencies; scale down non-user-facing replicas during off-peak to save cost.
- Quantization profile: we recommend 4-bit quant with per-channel scales for 70B to keep memory footprint manageable and latency predictable. Redwood Optimize can run an auto-profile to suggest safe quant knobs.
- Security: for Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we provide tenant isolation docs and audit trails.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-config.yml (detailed mapping of roles, node types, autoscaling triggers). I've also uploaded a short PPT to Drive: "EdgeOps - Redwood draft topology".

Proposed next meetings:
- 60-min infra deep-dive (SREs + runtime): Tue 11/23 09:00 or 10:30 PT (please confirm)
- Commercial review / MAP sync: Wed 11/24 11:00 PT (Marcus to lead)

If these numbers look reasonable, Marcus will follow with a capacity commit band and I will produce a one-page runbook for failover and on-call playbooks.

Cheers,
Diego
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
